transcript: so in the new spooky immersive experience from the creators of Sleep No More every audience member is barefoot there are moments of complete darkness and sometimes you're even on your hands and knees sometimes in confined spaces so needless to say it's definitely not for everybody Viola’s Roomis very different from what Punchdrunk is mostly known for there are no live actors and it's completely linear and guided so you can't wander or linger around the space Each audience member has a pair of headphones through which we hear this dark fairy tale narrated by Helena Bonham Carter which relates to the room that were in at any given time I found the whole thing pretty exhilarating and like there are no jump scares but it's eerie like I was pretty creeped out throughout a lot of the show I'll be honest and say that at the end of the show I did have a moment of like “oh is that it?” cause it is less than an hour long and some of it is up to interpretation so at first it show is actually about this girl who has like a nagging itch to return to this dark mystical place that she discovers and I feel very much the same about this show. if you feel like the show might be too much for you to handle based on some of the stuff I was talking about earlier I think that's totally fair but if you're kind of on the other side and you're thinking like oh I don't know like it's just an audio play like there's no live actors it's just an hour I don't know I would still urge you to give it a chance I paid £30 for it which at the time I thought was like a little bit high for what it was but especially given how much it has stayed with me I feel like it was definitely worth it It feels like immersive theater, like this would not just work as an audio play or as a walk through immersive experience the way they work together is essential and there are no live actors but it kind of feels like you are playing the character or one of the characters and that is kind of
